questions.statement: Which sentence uses the past simple correctly?
questions.context: Past simple regular verbs, San Juan, grado 11, W03.

options.text: They walked to the beach yesterday.
options.feedback: Correct. 'Walked' is the regular past simple, with the -ed suffix after a consonant.

options.text: They walk to the beach yesterday.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Walk' is the base form; the marker 'yesterday' requires the past simple with the -ed ending.

options.text: They are walked to the beach yesterday.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Are walked' mixes the present continuous with the past simple and is not a valid form.

options.text: They walking to the beach yesterday.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Walking' is the -ing form of the present continuous and can't take the place of the main verb in the past.

questions.explanation:
Los verbos regulares forman el pasado simple anadiendo -ed al verbo base. Es el unico tiempo verbal que se construye solo con la raiz del verbo, sin ningun auxiliar, por eso el orden sujeto mas verbo se mantiene intacto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'We ____ (study) for the exam all last week.'
questions.context: Past simple regular spelling, Ponce, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The consonant -y changes to -i, so writing 'studyed' doesn't follow any rule.
Incorrect. 'Study' is the present base form and lacks the -ed ending that the past simple requires.
Correct. A verb ending in a consonant plus -y changes the -y to -i before adding -ed.
Incorrect. The -e of the suffix is missing: the regular past simple always ends in -ed or -d.

questions.explanation:
La ortografia del pasado simple tiene una regla util para los verbos terminados en consonante y -y. En ese caso la -y se cambia por -i y despues se anade -ed, como en 'study' que da 'studied'. Si la vocal anterior es una a, se conserva la -y.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'He ____ (go) to Ponce last Saturday.'
questions.context: Past simple irregular verbs, Carolina, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Adding -ed to an irregular verb doesn't produce an English form; 'go' must be learned separately.
Correct. 'To go' is irregular and its past simple is 'went', without an -ed ending.
Incorrect. 'Gone' is the past participle, used with 'have' or in the passive, not as a main verb in the past simple.
Incorrect. 'Going' belongs to the present continuous and also needs the auxiliary 'was' to be valid.

questions.explanation:
Los verbos irregulares no siguen la regla de anadir -ed y deben aprenderse de memoria. Los mas frecuentes son 'to go', 'to see' y 'to take'. Una forma como 'goed' demuestra que el verbo es irregular y no se puede derivar.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct negative: 'I ____ (not / see) the doctor yesterday.'
questions.context: Past simple negative forms, Bayamon, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect. After 'didn't' the verb goes back to the base form, so it should be 'see', not 'saw'.
Incorrect. 'Don't' is the present simple negative, and the sentence already places the action in the past.
Incorrect. The auxiliary 'did' is missing, and it is required in every negative past simple sentence.
Correct. The negative past simple uses 'did not' or 'didn't' before the verb in its base form.

questions.explanation:
En pasado simple el negativo se forma siempre con 'did not' o 'didn't', y el verbo principal vuelve a su forma base. Esa es la trampa principal de la unidad: el auxiliar ya marca el pasado, asi que anadir la terminacion del pasado seria incorrecto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which question is correct?
questions.context: Past simple questions, Arecibo, grado 11, W03.

options.text: Do you finished the project last week?
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Do' is the present simple auxiliary, and the verb also has the wrong ending.

options.text: Did you finished the project last week?
options.feedback: Incorrect. After 'did' the verb goes back to the base form, so the -ed ending is unnecessary and makes the sentence invalid.

options.text: Was you finish the project last week?
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Was' belongs to the verb 'to be' and can't be followed by the main verb in its base form.

options.text: Did you finish the project last week?
options.feedback: Correct. A past simple question opens with 'Did', and the main verb stays in the base form.

questions.explanation:
Las preguntas de pasado simple se forman con 'did' al principio y el verbo principal en forma base. Igual que en el negativo, el auxiliar ya aporta la marca de pasado y el verbo no la repite. Este patron se repite en todas las preguntas de la unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'They ____ (be) at the party last night.'
questions.context: Past simple with to be, Humacao, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Was' goes with the first and third person singular, not with the plural subject 'they'.
Correct. With the subject 'they' the past of 'to be' is 'were', and 'last night' confirms the tense.
Incorrect. 'Are' is present, so it doesn't agree with the time marker 'last night'.
Incorrect. 'Be' is the base form of the verb and needs a conjugated form to work as the main verb.

questions.explanation:
El pasado simple de 'to be' tiene solo dos formas: 'was' para I, he, she e it, y 'were' para you, we, they. Es el verbo irregular mas frecuente del idioma y aparece en casi todos los ejercicios de pasado.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which is the correct past simple form of the verb 'to stop'?
questions.context: Past simple spelling rules, Aguadilla, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Correct. When the verb ends in a short stressed vowel plus a consonant, the consonant is doubled and then -ed is added.
Incorrect. Without doubling the -p, the word would lose its short vowel and sound different; the rule requires the double consonant.
Incorrect. 'Stoppes' doubles the -p and adds a final -e, and no past simple rule produces that form.
Incorrect. 'Stopt' doesn't exist; the regular past simple always ends in -ed or -d.

questions.explanation:
La duplicacion de consonante en pasado simple ocurre tras vocal breve tensa, como en 'stop' que da 'stopped' o 'plan' que da 'planned'. Si la vocal es larga no se duplica, como en 'look' que da 'looked' o 'call' que da 'called'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'She ____ (write) three emails last night.'
questions.context: Past simple with irregular verbs, Guayanilla, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Adding -ed to an irregular verb isn't correct English, and 'wrote' is the only accepted form.
Incorrect. 'Written' is the past participle, used in 'have written' and never on its own as a main verb in the past.
Correct. The past simple of 'to write' is 'wrote', which is often confused with 'to ride' but is spelled with -o-.
Incorrect. 'Write' is the base form and carries no past marker; the conjugated verb or the auxiliary 'did' is missing.

questions.explanation:
El pasado simple irregulares suele terminar en vocal y comparte terminacion con otros verbos. 'To write' y 'to ride' dan 'wrote' y 'rode', mientras que 'to speak' y 'to break' dan 'spoke' y 'broke'. Memorizar las familias completas es mas eficiente que aprenderlas sueltas.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct tag: 'He finished the exam, ____?'
questions.context: Past simple question tags, Trujillo Alto, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Doesn't' is the present simple auxiliary, and the main clause is in the past.
Incorrect. 'Wasn't' belongs to the verb 'to be', and here the main verb is 'finished'.
Correct. A positive statement takes a negative tag, and 'did' is the auxiliary that goes with the past simple.
Incorrect. The tag must reverse the polarity by placing the auxiliary before the pronoun, not after it.

questions.explanation:
El question tag del pasado simple se construye con 'did' seguido del pronombre y de la forma contracta 'not'. En afirmativo el tag es 'did he' y en negativo es 'didn't he'. El orden siempre es auxiliar, pronombre y negacion.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'They ____ (eat) at the restaurant before the concert.'
questions.context: Past simple with irregular verbs, Barceloneta, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Correct. The past simple of 'to eat' is 'ate', a completely irregular form that has to be memorized.
Incorrect. English never forms the past of 'eat' by adding -ed, because it is irregular.
Incorrect. 'Eaten' is the past participle, which needs 'have' in front of it to form the present perfect.
Incorrect. This is the base form; without 'did' or a conjugated form, the sentence does not express a specific past action.

questions.explanation:
Los verbos irregulares del pasado tienen tres familias principales. Los terminados en -t como 'eat' dan 'ate', los terminados en -o como 'go' dan 'went' y los terminados en -d como 'build' dan 'built'. Reconocer la familia acelera la memorizacion.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'We ____ (have) a good time at the carnival.'
questions.context: Past simple with to have, Maunabo, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Haved' does not exist in English; 'to have' is irregular and its past is 'had'.
Incorrect. Adding -ed to 'have' does not produce a valid form, even though 'have' works as an auxiliary in other tenses.
Incorrect. 'Hade' is not a past simple verb form; the past of 'to have' is always 'had'.
Correct. The past simple of 'to have' is 'had', the same form for all persons, singular and plural.

questions.explanation:
El pasado simple de 'to have' es 'had', y a diferencia de 'to be' no distingue entre singular y plural. Esa misma forma 'had' aparece tambien como auxiliar del pasado perfecto, por lo que conviene reconocer el contexto para no confundirlas.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'It ____ (not / be) cloudy yesterday afternoon.'
questions.context: Past simple with the verb to be, Yauco, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Weren't' goes with a plural subject, and the subject of the sentence is singular 'it'.
Correct. The past negative of 'to be' with the subject 'it' is formed with 'was not' or 'wasn't'.
Incorrect. 'Didn't' is only used with action verbs in the base form, never with 'to be'.
Incorrect. 'Isn't' is present; the time marker 'yesterday afternoon' requires the past form.

questions.explanation:
El pasado de 'to be' se niega con 'not' detras de la forma 'was' o 'were'. Los auxiliares 'did' no participan nunca con 'to be', porque ese verbo ya es irregular por completo y forma el pasado por sí mismo.

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'He ____ (carry) the boxes to the truck.'
questions.context: Past simple with spelling rules, Cayey, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The long vowel 'a' keeps the -y in the past, and spelling it 'caried' is a non-native speaker's mistake.
Correct. When a long vowel comes before the -y, the -y is kept and only -ed is added, as in 'carried'.
Incorrect. The -y is not changed to -i when the preceding vowel is an a, and 'caryed' is not an English form.
Incorrect. A verb ending in -y never adds -ed directly when the y is consonantal or preceded by a long vowel.

questions.explanation:
La -y del pasado simple se convierte en -i solo cuando la consonante o vocal anterior no es una 'a'. Si la -y va precedida de vocal larga se conserva, como en 'play' que da 'played' o 'enjoy' que da 'enjoyed'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'The committee ____ (decide) the date last Tuesday.'
questions.context: Past simple with irregular verbs, San Sebastian, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The vowel in 'decide' is long, so the -d is not doubled when adding -ed.
Incorrect. The final -d is missing, and the regular past simple always ends in -ed or -d.
Incorrect. A double -d does not follow any rule; the correct form is 'decided' with a single final -d.
Correct. 'Decided' is a regular past form ending in -ed, so the suffix does not change the pronunciation of the -d.

questions.explanation:
Cuando el verbo ya termina en -e o en -d, el pasado simple solo necesita la -d del sufijo. Asi 'decide' da 'decided', 'like' da 'liked' y 'need' da 'needed'. No hay que duplicar nada en estos casos.

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'I ____ (do) my homework before dinner yesterday.'
questions.context: Past simple with the verb to do, Camuy, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Doed' is not an English form; the past of 'to do' is 'did'.
Incorrect. 'Done' is the past participle and needs 'have' in front of it, as in 'I have done it'.
Correct. The past simple of 'to do' is 'did', with no -ed ending and no auxiliary in front.
Incorrect. This is the base form of the verb and does not express the past, and the sentence already contains 'yesterday'.

questions.explanation:
'To do' es uno de los verbos irregulares mas usados y su pasado simple es 'did'. Conviene no confundirlo con 'done', que es el participio pasado. La diferencia se ve en el auxiliar: solo el pasado usa 'did' como verbo principal.

questions.statement: Question: 'Did you call the doctor?' Answer: '____'
questions.context: Past simple in short answers, Luquillo, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Correct. The short answer repeats the auxiliary 'did' from the question, which is the expected form in the past simple.
Incorrect. 'Was' answers questions with 'to be' and does not match the auxiliary 'did' in the question.
Incorrect. It is a valid answer but not a short one; the expected form repeats the auxiliary, not the main verb.
Incorrect. 'Do' is the present simple short answer and does not match a question with 'did'.

questions.explanation:
Las respuestas cortas en pasado simple usan el mismo auxiliar que la pregunta. Como la pregunta abre con 'did', la respuesta abre con 'did' y el verbo principal se omite. Ese es el criterio para elegir entre 'did', 'was' y 'do'.

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'They ____ (break) the window when the ball hit it.'
questions.context: Past simple with irregular verbs, Toa Baja, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Correct. The past simple of 'to break' is 'broke', which shares its ending with 'to speak', 'to drive' and 'to rise'.
Incorrect. Adding -ed to an irregular verb does not produce a valid English form.
Incorrect. 'Broken' is the past participle, used in 'have broken', not on its own as a main verb.
Incorrect. This is the base form, and the sentence has no 'did', so there is no past marker at all.

questions.explanation:
La terminacion -oke del pasado irregular es muy productiva. La comparten 'to break', 'to speak', 'to drive', 'to wake' y 'to choose'. Identificar la familia evita tener que memorizar cada verbo por separado.

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'The students ____ (take) the exam on Monday morning.'
questions.context: Past simple with irregular verbs, Naguabo, grado 11, W03.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The verb 'to take' is irregular and does not take the regular past -ed ending.
Incorrect. 'Taken' is the past participle and requires the auxiliary 'have' to form the present perfect.
Incorrect. 'Taked' does not exist in English; the correct past simple form is 'took'.
Correct. The past simple of 'to take' is 'took', an irregular form that looks like the present but has a long vowel.

questions.explanation:
Varios verbos irregulares forman su pasado con una vocal larga en lugar de terminacion. 'To take' da 'took', 'to speak' da 'spoke' y 'to break' da 'broke'. Son las formas que mas errores producen por parecerse a las del presente.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the past simple of the verb 'to be' correctly?
questions.context: Past simple with the verb to be, Hatillo, grado 11, W03.

options.text: She didn't ready for the test.
options.feedback: Incorrect. After 'did' the verb goes back to the base form, and 'ready' is an adjective, not a verb.

options.text: She wasn't ready for the test.
options.feedback: Correct. 'Wasn't' is the contracted form of 'was not' and is the past form for a singular subject.

options.text: She wasn't be ready for the test.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The past of 'to be' is already a complete form, so the base form 'be' after it is unnecessary.

options.text: She isn't ready for the test yesterday.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Isn't' is present and contradicts the time marker 'yesterday' in the sentence.

questions.explanation:
Con 'to be' el pasado simple es 'was' o 'were' y no lleva auxiliar 'did' delante. El verbo 'to be' tiene su propio sistema de pasado, por eso un adjetivo como 'ready' se coloca directamente despues sin ninguna forma verbal adicional.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is correct?
questions.context: Past simple with prepositions of time, Yabucoa, grado 11, W03.

options.text: She moves to Mayaguez two years ago.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Moves' is present simple and does not agree with an expression that places the action in the past.

options.text: She is moving to Mayaguez two years ago.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The present continuous cannot be used with 'ago', because the action has already happened and is not in progress.

options.text: She moved to Mayaguez two years ago.
options.feedback: Correct. 'Two years ago' is a past time expression, and the verb 'moved' matches that time marker.

options.text: She moved to Mayaguez two years ago tomorrow.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Ago' and 'tomorrow' contradict each other; the two time expressions cannot appear together.

questions.explanation:
Las expresiones de tiempo guian la eleccion del tiempo verbal. 'Ago', 'yesterday' y 'last' exigen pasado simple, mientras que 'tomorrow' y 'next week' piden futuro. Reconocer la marca antes de conjugar evita la mayoria de los errores de esta unidad.
